newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai Bangchak in talks to buy Oman after tender.
newsitem.headline: Thai Bangchak in talks to buy Oman after tender.

text.p: Bangchak Petroleum Plc is negotiating to buy Oman crude oil after it decided not to award any crudes other than Tapis in its November purchase tender, industry sources said on Tuesday.
The tender to buy 500,000 barrels of Middle East grades and 600,000 barrels of light sweet Far East grades was valid until Thursday last week.
Industry sources said Bangchak awarded 600,000 barrels of Tapis at $1.15 premium over benchmark Tapis quotes to a trader.
But offers of four Oman, one Dubai and one Iranian cargoes were not awarded by the time the offers expired at the validity date on Thursday, the sources said.
However, Bangchak, which regularly runs Oman crude, was negotiating with several traders to buy spot cargoes of Oman crude, the sources said.
For the past two weeks, Oman crude was being traded against Dubai quotes because traders said its value had fallen substantially below its official selling price set by Oman.
But this weekend Oman released a September term price of $21.20, giving a 78-cent premium over Dubai compared with a month earlier 96-cent premium.
On Friday, a major acquired a cargo of Oman at MPM less one cent and traders said the same major bought another cargo on Monday at MPM plus two cents.
